name: Port Moresby Nature Park
bio: Port Moresby wildlife park with tree kangaroos, cassowaries, birds of paradise and a walk-through WWII aviary.
note: Wildlife and botanical park (formerly the National Capital Botanical Gardens) with tree kangaroos, cassowaries, birds of paradise, a WWII walk-through aviary and gardens.

facts.fact: 30-acre wildlife and botanical park on Goro Kaeage Road with over 500 animals; attractions include a WWII walk-through aviary, tree kangaroo trail, Reptile Haus, cassowary corridor and bird of paradise precinct
Formerly the National Capital Botanical Gardens; the adjoining National Orchid Garden is a separate site

2026 fee brochure: operating hours 9 am - 4 pm every day; entry for tourists K22 adult, K17 student with ID, K12 child 3-12; local residents K12 adult; guided tour K66 for a group of 1-4 people (K15 for 5 or more) on top of entry

name: National Museum and Art Gallery
bio: Waigani museum of over 30,000 objects, from traditional boats to Sepik art, with WWII planes and tanks outside.
note: Museum: PNG's national museum in Waigani, with carvings, beads, traditional boats, cultural objects and WWII relics outside.

facts.fact: National museum in Waigani on Independence Drive next to the National Parliament, with sculptures, beads, traditional boats and cultural objects
Photography not permitted inside; newer objects and WWII remains (planes, tanks) sit outside
Collection of over 30,000 objects; permanent displays on traditional warfare, body art and the Sepik
Wikivoyage (updated Jun 2019): Mon-Sat 9AM-3PM, Sun 1-3PM; free during the week, K10 at weekends

name: Bomana War Cemetery
bio: Commonwealth war cemetery 19 km north-east of Port Moresby, with 3,824 graves, many from the Kokoda campaign.
note: War cemetery: the largest WWII Commonwealth cemetery in PNG, 3,824 graves, mostly from the Kokoda campaign; free and open daily, 19 km out of town.

facts.fact: CWGC cemetery 19 km north-east of Port Moresby on the road to Nine Mile (Pilgrims Way side road) with 3,824 Commonwealth burials, many from the Kokoda campaign; 699 unidentified
Open daily and free; visitors asked to speak quietly and not step on graves
City commission lists the park open daily 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM (Wikivoyage says 9AM-4PM)

name: National Parliament of Papua New Guinea
bio: Waigani's Parliament House, styled on a Maprik haus tambaran spirit house, with group tours on weekdays.
note: Landmark: the parliament building in Waigani, designed on a Maprik haus tambaran; visitors see the exterior, with guided tours outside sitting days.

facts.fact: Parliament House, built in the style of a Maprik haus tambaran (spirit house from East Sepik), dating from 1984
Open to the public on weekdays (except public holidays); parliamentary staff do guided tours for groups of visitors; public gallery overlooks the chamber when sitting

name: Gordons Market
bio: Gordon's largest produce market in Port Moresby, selling vegetables from other provinces; go with a known driver.
note: Market: a daily city market in Gordons with produce, betel nut, crafts and bilums; best visited in the morning with a guide.

facts.fact: Largest of the major produce markets in the Gordon area of Port Moresby; vegetables and produce from other provinces and abroad are sold
Wikivoyage advises arranging transport via a hotel and getting the driver's number to call for the return trip

name: Loloata Island
bio: Private resort island in Bootless Bay with snorkelling and diving; day visits by ferry from Tahira, booked ahead.
note: Island: a private island resort in Bootless Inlet, 20-30 minutes by boat from Port Moresby, with snorkelling, diving, kayaks and day visits.

facts.fact: Private island resort in Bootless Bay; day passes give access to private beaches, pools and restaurants; round-trip ferry from Tahira terminal included
Day visitors must book at least 24 hours ahead (no walk-ins), bring ID, no outside food or drink, no guest-room access; free parking at Tahira; charter boat K300 one way for up to 8
FAQ: boat trip to the island K100 per person; 29 dive sites and snorkelling nearby, including Lion Island depending on currents
Day visit sheet: kayaks K20-30 per hour, stand-up board K20 per hour, banana boat K30; lunch at Sea Breeze restaurant

name: Kerema
bio: Gulf Province's capital on the Gulf of Papua coast, a basic base with a few hotels, reached by road or air.
note: Town: the capital of Gulf Province on the Gulf of Papua coast, a basic base for the Gulf with a few hotels, reached by the Hiritano Highway or by air.

name: Kikori
bio: Small fishing town on the Kikori River delta, used as a base for birdwatching in the delta.
note: Town: a small fishing centre on the Kikori River delta, a good birdwatching base with Delta Lodge.

name: Goroka
bio: Eastern Highlands capital and the region's main hub, the base for the Goroka Show, Asaro Mudmen and Mount Michael.
note: Town: provincial capital of Eastern Highlands and the base for the Goroka Show, Asaro Mudmen and Mount Michael; the region's main hub (base).

name: Mount Hagen
bio: Western Highlands capital and air hub, the base for visits to Kuk, Baiyer River and the town's market.
note: Town: provincial capital of Western Highlands and the regional air hub (Kagamuga Airport); base for Kuk, Hagen Show, Baiyer River and Mount Hagen Market.

name: Kainantu
bio: Market town on the Highlands Highway between Lae and Goroka, with a cultural centre and local pottery.
note: Town: market town on the Highlands Highway with the Eastern Highlands Cultural Centre and pottery; a stop between Lae and Goroka.

name: Mendi
bio: Southern Highlands capital and gateway to Lake Kutubu and Mount Giluwe, with a Friday and Saturday market.
note: Town: provincial capital of Southern Highlands; gateway to Lake Kutubu and Mount Giluwe, with a Friday and Saturday market.

name: Kundiawa
bio: Simbu Province capital and the departure point for the Mount Wilhelm climb, reached via Keglsugl.
note: Town: capital of Simbu (Chimbu) Province; the departure point for the Mount Wilhelm climb, reached from Keglsugl.

name: Mount Wilhelm
bio: PNG's highest mountain at 4,509 m, climbed with a local guide from Keglsugl, with a night on the mountain.
note: Mountain: Papua New Guinea's highest peak (4,509 m), climbed by guided treks from Keglsugl (Simbu) or Ambullua (Western Highlands).

facts.fact: PNG's highest mountain at 4,509 m; the tourism authority says it is accessible but not easy and guides should always be taken; good road to Keglsugl village from Kundiawa, with huts and lodges at the base
Base camp Keglsugl is about five hours by road from Goroka; the climb involves an overnight stay on the mountain; local guide is essential; temperatures below freezing at the summit
Operator packages (e.g. an Ambullua-route traverse) start around AUD 3,799 per person, bundling permits, community fees and guides

name: Mount Giluwe
bio: Extinct volcano in the Southern Highlands, second-highest in PNG, climbed with a guide in about a day.
note: Mountain: second-highest peak in PNG (4,368 m), a shield volcano with guided climbs, in Southern Highlands.

facts.fact: Second-highest mountain in PNG at 4,367 m, an extinct volcano in the Southern Highlands; the tourism authority says trekking takes roughly an entire day and requires a guide; terrain is sub-alpine grassland, rainforest and moss forest
Operators use local teams and landowner (Molgi/Molge village) negotiation for access; typically drier May-October
Trips usually start from Mount Hagen or Mendi

name: Lake Kutubu
bio: Ramsar-listed upland lake south-west of Mendi, home to ten fish found nowhere else, with villages reached by canoe.
note: Lake: 800 m upland lake, about 50 km southwest of Mendi, with Ramsar status and endemic fish; reached by road and boat.

facts.fact: 800 m lake, second-largest in PNG, about 50 km south-west of Mendi; ten of its 14 fish found only there; villages around the lake can be visited by canoe
Ramsar site; oil and gas development has brought road links and regular flights
Wikipedia: second-largest lake in PNG and the largest upland body of water, 51.84 km2

name: Kavieng
bio: New Ireland's capital at the island's northern tip, a gateway for diving, surfing, fishing and boat trips, with wartime history.
note: Town: capital of New Ireland Province at the northern tip of the island, the main air and sea gateway and base for diving, surfing, fishing and island boat trips; WWII bombing and occupation history.

name: Lihir Group
bio: Gold-mining island group off New Ireland, reached by daily flight from Port Moresby, with Kunaye Beach Resort.
note: Island group: Lihir, Mahur, Masahet and Sanambiet off the New Ireland coast, a gold-mining island group reached by scheduled flights from Namatanai; named as one of the province's islands, with little visitor infrastructure.

facts.fact: Island group off New Ireland (Lihir, Mali, Mahur, Masahet, Sanambiet) in the Bismarck Archipelago
Gold found in the early 1980s; the mine holds an estimated 40 million ounces; Londolovit is the mining town with Kunaye Beach Resort; Air Niugini flies Port Moresby to Lihir daily

name: Lorengau
bio: Manus Province capital beside Seeadler Harbour, with a market, garamut dance tradition and sago village visits.
note: Town: capital of Manus Province on the edge of Seeadler Harbour, with a market, a garamut dance tradition, sago village visits and the Harbourside Hotel tours.

name: Manus Island
bio: Largest of the Admiralty Islands, with Lorengau on Seeadler Harbor, WWII relics and reefs for diving; reached by air.
note: Island: the main island of the Admiralty group, where Lorengau, Seeadler Harbour and the WWII sites are; the province is named for it.

facts.fact: Largest of the Admiralty Islands, 2,100 km2, forested volcanic island; Lorengau is the provincial capital on Seeadler Harbor
WWII relics remain in Lorengau; Americans retook the islands in 1944 and built a large base at Seeadler Harbor; reefs reached by outboard or canoe for diving and fishing

name: Buka Island
bio: Island where flights arrive for Bougainville, with Buka Passage boat trips and a road circling the island.
note: Island: Buka Island, the arrival point for Bougainville by air and the Buka Passage boat trips; the island has the airport, the tourist office and most places to stay.

facts.fact: Arrival point for Bougainville by air; Buka town holds the airport and most places to stay; the Buka Passage between Buka and Bougainville is a key visitor attraction
Air Niugini flies Port Moresby to Buka daily except Sunday; a short water taxi crosses to the main island; a gravelled road circles Buka Island
Sohano Island a short boat ride away is a former colonial headquarters and WWII Japanese seaplane base (from a search-result summary; page not read)

name: Buka
bio: Bougainville's busiest town, with a market, boats across Buka Passage and waterfront restaurants.
note: Town: Buka, the most bustling town in Bougainville and the seat of government since the civil war, with the Buka Market, the Buka Passage boats and waterfront restaurants.

name: Sohano Island
bio: Island 10 minutes by boat from Buka Market, with a mona canoe, an ANZAC memorial and views across the passage.
note: Island: Sohano, the most visited island in the Buka Passage, with simple eateries and places to stay, a Japanese war memorial and plane wreck on its northern tip and a short K2 boat ride from Buka.

facts.text: Sohano is a 10-minute boat trip across the Buka Passage from the harbour beside Buka Market; it was the provincial capital for several decades after WWII.
Walking the island you find a large traditional mona canoe, an ANZAC memorial to fallen soldiers, old trees and views across the passage.
Wikivoyage describes a Japanese war memorial and plane wreck on the northern tip, and Tchibo Rock, said by local legend to have magical properties.
Commuter boats cost about K2: go to the beach and ask the drivers who is leaving next. Simple eateries and places to stay are on the island.
Bougainville EcoVentures runs a guided walking tour of Sohano.

note_discrepancy: Tourism body mentions an ANZAC memorial; Wikivoyage mentions a Japanese war memorial and plane wreck on the north tip. Use whichever the writer can keep to the tourism body's wording.

name: Mount Balbi
bio: Active volcano and Bougainville's highest peak at 2,715 m, climbed over three days from Wakunai with a local guide.
note: Mountain: Mount Balbi (2,715 m), an active volcano in the Emperor Range, the highest in the Bougainville chain, reached by a three-day trek from Wakunai.

facts.text: Mount Balbi (local name Tutue) is the highest point on Bougainville at 2,715 m; the trek climbs a steep track through varying forest types.
Near the summit are sulphur vents, a turquoise blue lake and steaming hot springs; the volcano is classed as active but has not erupted in historic time.
The usual route is a three-day hike started from Wakunai on the east coast, where guides are available; one trekker reports over 20 hours of walking across three nights.
Treks cross private land, so a local guide is essential; local operators include Rotokas Ecotourism (Wakunai) and Bougainville Experience Tours (Arawa).
An extension across the Emperor Range to the west coast takes about a week.

note_discrepancy: Mount Balbi is 2,715 m per the tourism body and Wikipedia; Wikivoyage gives 2,685 m.

name: Nissan Island
bio: Crescent island around a turquoise lagoon, with WWII airstrip relics; a four-hour boat ride from Buka.
note: Island: Nissan (Green Island), about 100 km north of Buka, with an American WWII airstrip, relics and a guest house with no telephone booking.

facts.text: The Green Islands, commonly called the Nissan Islands, lie about 94 km north-west of Buka Island and are reached by about a four-hour boat ride from Buka Town.
Nissan is a crescent enclosing a turquoise lagoon, ringed by coral reefs; visitors are welcomed with a traditional ceremony.

WWII relics include the Allied-built airstrip and island road, and the concrete bases of a supply warehouse and water reservoir known as Nixon's swimming pool, where Richard Nixon served as a supply officer; some unexploded bombs remain live.
Dudualen Beach at Balil Village on the northern tip is described as good for snorkelling and diving.
There are three guesthouses on the island that cannot be booked ahead because there is no phone service, and they receive very few guests.
Travel on a boat registered with the National Maritime Safety Authority and check the weather service first.

name: Samarai
bio: Former colonial port island at the entrance to Milne Bay, 20 minutes to walk round, reached by boat from Alotau.
note: Island: former colonial capital and trading port at the entrance to Milne Bay, a 20-minute walk round, with ruins of its boom-town past and a National Historical Heritage Island listing; reached by boat from Alotau.

facts.text: Samarai is a 59-acre island at the entrance to Milne Bay that was once an important stopover between Australia and East Asia; in 1902 it exported three times as much by value as Port Moresby.
Little remains of the town because it was destroyed in WWII; the island was declared a National Historical Heritage Island in 2006.
It takes about 20 minutes to walk around the island.
Public dinghies reportedly leave from Sanderson Bay in Alotau, usually in the afternoon, and return the next morning; one traveller paid 50 kina return and the trip took over three hours.
The provincial tourism page lists Samarai as a historic colonial-era port with preserved architecture and a popular island-hopping stop.

name: Tawali
bio: Rainforest headland with a fringing reef and dive resort, reached by sea, with over 60 dive sites within an hour.
note: Dive site: reef and drop-offs at Tawali on the coast near Alotau, named by the PNG tourism authority as a world-renowned Milne Bay dive site; reached by boat, with the Tawali Leisure and Dive Resort on the bluff above.

facts.text: Tawali is a rainforest headland with a fringing reef, reached only by sea; the resort has run since 1994 and offers more than 60 dive sites within an hour.
Dives include coral gardens, walls, wrecks, muck diving and the only underwater post box in Papua New Guinea.

The resort's own 2026 tour rates range from US$35-60 per person for the skull caves and waterfall walk, to US$48-75 for coral garden snorkelling (price falls with group size); dive packages start at US$2,900 for seven nights with 15 dives.
The national tourism authority names Tawali, Deacon's Reef, Wahoo Point and Gonubalabala as world-renowned Milne Bay dive sites.

name: Normanby Island
bio: Mountainous D'Entrecasteaux island of rainforest trails and birdwatching, reached by boat from Alotau.
note: Island: unspoilt D'Entrecasteaux island with trekking trails, rainforest waterfalls and birdwatching (including the Goldie's bird-of-paradise), with very limited accommodation.

facts.text: Normanby is the southernmost and a mountainous, L-shaped island of the D'Entrecasteaux group, about 73 km long.
Wikivoyage lists Goodenough and Normanby as totally unspoilt islands for exploring and birdwatching, with very limited accommodation.

The provincial tourism page names trails on Normanby and Fergusson as rainforest hikes with waterfalls, caves and birdwatching, and lists the D'Entrecasteaux Islands as home of the rare Goldie's bird-of-paradise.

name: Fergusson Island
bio: Largest of the D'Entrecasteaux Islands, a geothermal rainforest island with birdwatching, reached only by boat.
note: Island: geothermal volcanic island reached only by boat, with trekking trails and birdwatching for a rare bird-of-paradise and the Curl-crested Manucode; its hot springs at Deidei are listed separately.

facts.text: Fergusson is the largest of the D'Entrecasteaux Islands (1,437 sq km), mostly mountainous rainforest with three large volcanoes.
Wikivoyage calls it a geothermal island with good birdwatching, including a rare species of bird-of-paradise and the Curl-crested Manucode, reached only by boat.
The D'Entrecasteaux islands still show volcanic activity, especially around Dobu and Fergusson.

name: Trobriand Islands
bio: Raised coral atolls with white beaches and preserved traditional dancing, reached by twice-weekly flight.
note: Island group: the Kiriwina Islands, raised coral atolls in the north of Milne Bay known as the Islands of Love, with yam-harvest dancing, village stays, the Kula ring and white beaches; reached by a twice-weekly PNG Air flight from Alotau.

facts.text: The Trobriand (Kiriwina) Islands are raised coral atolls in northern Milne Bay with white-sand beaches, coral lagoons and rainforest; about 12,000 people live mostly on Kiriwina.

The culture is matrilineal and centred on yam cultivation; a distinct version of cricket introduced by missionaries is played, and traditional dancing is preserved, especially during the yam harvest in June or July.
The islands are part of the Kula Ring exchange network.
PNG Air flies twice weekly from Port Moresby via Alotau on a Twin Otter; Air Niugini no longer flies there. Lodges include Kiriwina Lodge and Butia Lodge.

name: Louisiade Archipelago
bio: About 100 islands ringed by coral reefs, known for diving and visited mainly by yacht; ask before fishing.
note: Archipelago: about 100 islands in the far southeast of Milne Bay, a diver's paradise and yachting destination with coral reefs; few visitors and reached mainly by private yacht, so a region rather than a single stop.

facts.text: The Louisiade Archipelago is ten larger volcanic islands and about 90 smaller coral islands, many fringed by reefs.
It is renowned for coral reefs and diving and receives very few tourists apart from passing yachts; it is difficult to reach.
Communities live a subsistence life and almost everything is privately owned, so ask permission before fishing or taking anything; trading goods with canoes is common.
Islands include Misima, the Deboyne Islands, Calvados Chain, Duchateau group, Sudest and Rossel.

name: Misima Island
bio: Most accessible Louisiade island, with quiet beaches and a gold mine closed in 2004; reached by air from Alotau.
note: Island: the most populated and most accessible Louisiade island, served by air to Bwagaoia with a guest house; a closed gold mine and island-hopping stop named by the PNG tourism authority.

facts.text: Misima is the most populated and most accessible island of the Louisiade Archipelago, with about 5,000 people.
A gold mine opened in 1990 briefly changed island life and closed in 2004.
Airlines PNG connects Alotau with Misima twice weekly (per Wikivoyage); the tourism authority lists Misima among the popular island-hopping stops with quiet beaches.
The provincial tourism page names Misima as known for natural beauty and quiet beaches.

name: Goodenough Island
bio: Volcanic D'Entrecasteaux island rising to Mount Vineuo, with rainforest and birdwatching; reached from Alotau.
note: Island: volcanic island of the D'Entrecasteaux group with rainforest, waterfalls, Mount Vineuo and good birdwatching; named as an unspoilt island to explore and a tour destination from Alotau.

facts.text: Goodenough is the westernmost large D'Entrecasteaux island, 39 by 26 km, rising sharply to Mount Vineuo at 2,536 m.
Wikivoyage names Goodenough and Normanby as totally unspoilt islands for exploring and birdwatching with very limited accommodation; active geothermal fields are on Goodenough.
Tours reach Goodenough from Alotau; the tourism authority describes it as mountainous terrain and traditional village life.

name: Coastwatchers Lighthouse
bio: Working harbour lighthouse in Madang, also the memorial to WWII coastwatchers who reported Japanese movements.
note: Landmark: working lighthouse on Madang harbour, a memorial to the WWII coastwatchers.

facts.text: A working lighthouse on Madang harbour that serves as the Coastwatchers Memorial.
The coastwatchers were mainly Australians who stayed in New Guinea after the Japanese invasion and, with local helpers, reported on Japanese ship and plane movements at great personal risk.

name: Madang Central Market
bio: Busy central market in Madang where people bring Highlands produce to sell, mostly fruit and vegetables.
note: Market: busy local market in the centre of Madang, open daily, with produce brought in from the Highlands.

facts.text: A busy local market in the centre of Madang where people come from the Highlands with produce to sell.
Wikivoyage gives it as open every day except Sunday in one place and daily in another; it mainly sells fruit and vegetables, with a few bags, necklaces and t-shirts.
Buses to nearby towns leave from the central bus station next to the market.
